Incident Bot: [AUTO-PAGER] gpu-dyn-1 pool: sustained KV cache evictions -> spike in CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL (rate 24/min, threshold 10/min). Auto-shedder triggered. Paging #eng-oncall and running dynamic-autopager playbook. https://runbooks/internal/gpu-autopager :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Pager duty alert fired (PD-87321). Urgency: high. Notified primary oncall.
Alex Chen: ack. I'm looking at the pool now. seeing repeated: 
```
CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes
kvcache_evictions: 93% (5m)
active_infers: 182 -> spike
```
Maria Rios: oncall handover in 5m (wrapping). tagging @Sophie for routing. Is customer-facing traffic affected?
Jamal Patel: quick check — traces show >60% of requests to model-x are getting fallback to smaller variant but latency spike for some tenants. Not fatal but error rate rising.
Sophie Liu: thanks. I'm going to initiate emergency route to cpu-fallback for non-latency-critical tenants and scale down batch sizes for gpu-dyn-1. Can someone run the drain command?
Alex Chen: running drain on pool gpu-dyn-1 to stop new allocations:
```
# drain GPU pool
infractl pools drain --name gpu-dyn-1 --reason "kvcache-evict-spike"
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-dyn-1-proxy --replicas=0
```
Infra Runner: drain accepted, nodes marked draining in cluster 'us-west-2a'. Starting graceful eviction. ETA ~ 45s for inflight requests.
Jamal Patel: also lowering continuous-batching window for model-x to reduce memory pressure:
```
redwood-config set model-x.batch.window 8ms
redwood-config set model-x.kvcache.threshold 0.6
```
Maria Rios: notifying PD escalation policy to spin up reserved-dedicated fallback (if drain doesn't stabilize in 3m). PagerDuty: escalate if no ack from secondary.
PagerDuty: Escalation to secondary oncall (Sophie Liu) sent.
Alex Chen: seeing immediate drop in new CUDA_ALLOC_FAILs after drain started. kvcache_evictions trending down to 60% in the last minute. Memory alloc failures <= 5/min now.
Sophie Liu: routing change applied for non-critical tenants: `traffic-route set model-x cpu-fallback --match "tenant:non-critical"`. Watch for correctness.
Jamal Patel: quick sanity logs show one customer (tenant-id: 98a) had a few 503s during the switch. Maria, can you capture scope and send to support?
Maria Rios: noted. I opened a support ticket and pinged AMs. Short blip ~2m affecting a small subset. Will include logs and timeline.
Alex Chen: starting post-action snapshot for the pool and saving debug bundle:
```
infractl debug bundle --pool gpu-dyn-1 --out /tmp/gpu-dyn-1-6000012345.tar.gz
```
Incident Bot: Runbook checkpoint: mitigation applied (drain + reduce batch + cpu routing). Monitor for 10m.
Sophie Liu: confirming stabilization, kvcache_evictions 22% now, no new CUDA errors in last 90s. Recommend keeping pool drained and scheduling controlled repro for postmortem.
Jamal Patel: +1. Will open an incident ticket and assign follow-up to eng-runtime for KV cache telemetry improvements.
Alex Chen: marking incident as mitigated in the thread. I'll keep watch for 10 more minutes then update PD.
PagerDuty: PD-87321 acknowledged by Alex Chen. Holding escalation.
Incident Bot: Auto-pager resolved: condition cleared for gpu-dyn-1. Pool remains drained per operator. Suggested next steps: postmortem, add finer-grained thresholds, consider backoff on continuous-batching when eviction>50%.
Maria Rios: adding customer impact notes to the ticket and scheduling a 30m warp-down with runtime team.
Alex Chen: thanks team. closing loop here — will create the postmortem doc after follow-up. :white_check_mark:
